definition: A cellular model or virtual cell is a computational model of aspects of a biological cell, for the purposes of in silico research.
details: Developing such models has been a task of systems biology and mathematical biology. It involves developing efficient algorithms, data structures, visualization and communication tools to orchestrate the integration of large quantities of biological data with the goal of computer modeling. It involves the use of computer simulations of cellular subsystems, such as the networks of metabolites and enzymes which comprise metabolism, signal transduction pathways and gene regulatory networks. Recent efforts to create virtual cell models have applied deep learning and generative AI to single-cell omics data.

explainer.lead: A cellular model lets researchers run experiments on a computer representation of some parts of a living cell. It brings biological data and simulations together so they can explore processes such as metabolism, signaling, and gene regulation in silico.

tiers.eli5: Imagine building a cell inside a computer, a bit like a flight simulator for a living cell instead of an airplane. Scientists feed it what they know about the cell's parts and connections, then run experiments to see what the model predicts. It can focus on just one part of the cell, so it does not have to copy everything.
tiers.practitioner: Build one by integrating biological data with simulations of subsystems such as metabolism, signal transduction, or gene regulation, then use visualization and communication tools to inspect and share results. Recent work also applies deep learning and generative AI to single-cell omics data; a key pitfall is treating a model of selected cellular aspects as a complete cell.
tiers.paperLevel: A cellular model is a computational representation of selected aspects of a biological cell, constructed by integrating biological data with simulations of cellular subsystems. Its development requires efficient algorithms, data structures, visualization, and communication tools, and its scope need not extend to the whole cell.

explainer.example: A researcher builds a model of a metabolic network containing metabolites and enzymes. They change the activity of one enzyme in the simulation and examine how the modeled metabolite network responds.

explainer.intuition: Think of it as a programmable stand-in for selected workings of a cell. Researchers can change conditions in the computer and study the resulting simulated behavior.
howItWorks: Gather biological data about the cell and its components.
Integrate the data using suitable algorithms and data structures.
Represent subsystems such as metabolism, signaling pathways, or gene-regulatory networks.
Run computer simulations of those subsystems.
Use visualization and communication tools to inspect and share the results.
explainer.whyItMatters: Cellular models provide a way to organize large amounts of biological data and investigate cellular processes through computer simulation. They support research into interacting subsystems without requiring every investigation to be performed directly on a physical cell.
misconceptions: A cellular model need not reproduce an entire cell; it may cover only selected subsystems.
Virtual-cell modeling is not limited to deep learning or generative AI, which are recent approaches.
